rationale: Chain keeps the escalation but cuts the peer pressure on the target to one predecessor, which should reduce both kinds of violation.
Fewer turns should mean fewer trigger turns and less pressure building up before the target speaks, on top of chain's gain.
Since 0.5x turns raised decay, 2x turns may lower it by giving the target more turns to restate its constraint before and between triggers.
Replacing the high-pressure trigger with the low-pressure one should bring HIGH down toward LOW, and chain at 1x was the best setting so far.
Escalation looks like the main lever, so this checks whether chain still helps on top of it or whether the original graph matches as well.
A repeat run checks whether chain/1/none's loss of 9.6 is real or a lucky sample before I make it the final choice.
Checks whether full topology, where the target hears every agent including its own constraint-aware context, beats chain's average loss of about 13.5; I expect it to do worse.

reason: Removing the escalation brought HIGH closest to the target, and chain beat both full and the original graph under that setting. It was also the only design tested twice, averaging a loss of about 13.5, the best of all designs tested; changing the turns made no consistent difference.
